tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What are the speakers most probably doing?

options.A: Preparing for a job interview.
options.B: Writing a work report together.
options.C: Going through a couple of issues the company faces.
options.D: Discussing the woman’s annual performance review.

questions.cn: 两位说话人最可能在做什么？

optionsCn.A: 准备求职面试。
optionsCn.B: 一起写一份工作报告。
optionsCn.C: 讨论公司面临的几个问题。
optionsCn.D: 讨论女士的年度绩效评估。

questions.stem: What does the woman say she appreciates?

options.A: The overall culture of the company.
options.B: The instruction from her supervisor.
options.C: The honesty of the manager.
options.D: The recognition of her merits.

questions.cn: 女士说她感谢什么？

optionsCn.A: 公司整体的文化氛围。
optionsCn.B: 她的主管给出的指导。
optionsCn.C: 经理的坦诚。
optionsCn.D: 对她优点的认可。

questions.stem: What has given rise to some complaints about the woman?

options.A: Her inadequate language proficiency.
options.B: Her inability to interact with colleagues properly.
options.C: Her inappropriate behavior at company meetings.
options.D: Her simplistic approach to dealing with others.

questions.cn: 是什么引起了一些针对女士的意见？

optionsCn.A: 她语言能力不足。
optionsCn.B: 她无法与同事恰当相处。
optionsCn.C: 她在公司会议上的不当行为。
optionsCn.D: 她与人打交道的方式过于简单化。

questions.stem: Why doesn’t the woman like to write long emails?

options.A: To avoid offending the recipients.
options.B: To show her unique writing style.
options.C: To save time.
options.D: To be frank.

questions.cn: 女士为什么不喜欢写长邮件？

optionsCn.A: 为了不冒犯收件人。
optionsCn.B: 为了展示她独特的写作风格。
optionsCn.C: 为了节省时间。
optionsCn.D: 为了坦率。

lines.t: Okay, then, this here is your yearly performance review.
lines.cn: 好，那么，这就是你的年度绩效评估。

lines.t: You’ve been with the company for 3 years and under my direct supervision for the past 12 months.
lines.cn: 你在公司三年了，过去 12 个月由我直接管理。

lines.t: Your report is mostly good.
lines.cn: 你的报告总体不错。

lines.t: But there are a couple of issues we must discuss.
lines.cn: 但有几个问题我们必须谈一谈。

lines.t: The report is yours to take with you.
lines.cn: 报告你可以带走。

lines.t: We’ll go through the main points together now.
lines.cn: 我们现在一起过一遍要点。

lines.t: And you can comb through it in greater detail later.
lines.cn: 之后你可以更仔细地逐条看。

lines.t: Do you have any questions before we start?
lines.cn: 开始之前你有什么问题吗？

lines.t: No, sir.
lines.cn: 没有，先生。

lines.t: I’ll get straight to it then.
lines.cn: 那我就直接开始了。

lines.t: It is evident that you are a hard worker.
lines.cn: 很明显，你工作很努力。

lines.t: You are punctual and industrious.
lines.cn: 你守时、勤勉。

lines.t: Furthermore, you have strong analytical skills and attention to detail.
lines.cn: 此外，你有很强的分析能力和对细节的关注。

lines.t: The company, myself included, are happy with your productivity and overall performance.
lines.cn: 公司和我本人都对你的工作效率和整体表现满意。

lines.t: Thank you.
lines.cn: 谢谢。

lines.t: I appreciate the recognition.
lines.cn: 我很感谢这份认可。

lines.t: Do you agree, then, with this depiction so far?
lines.cn: 那么，你同意到目前为止的这些描述吗？

lines.t: Yeah, it’s a little simplistic, perhaps.
lines.cn: 嗯，也许有点过于简单了。

lines.t: But that’s to be expected from this kind of evaluation.
lines.cn: 但这种评估大概也就这样。

lines.t: Sure.
lines.cn: 当然。

lines.t: Would you want to add anything?
lines.cn: 你想补充点什么吗？

lines.t: Your comments can be added to the report if you wish.
lines.cn: 如果你愿意，你的意见可以写进报告。

lines.t: Oh, there’s no need.
lines.cn: 哦，不用了。

lines.t: It’s a flattering portrayal, really.
lines.cn: 说实话，这已经是很抬举人的描述了。

lines.t: Thank you, though.
lines.cn: 不过还是谢谢你。

lines.t: Okay.
lines.cn: 好。

lines.t: This leads me to the not-so-good part.
lines.cn: 接下来就是不太好听的部分了。

lines.t: This mostly centers around one behavioral aspect—your ability to work with others.
lines.cn: 这主要集中在一个行为方面——你和他人协作的能力。

lines.t: I see.
lines.cn: 我明白了。

lines.t: Yes.
lines.cn: 是的。

lines.t: As you already know, over the last several months, there have been some complaints raised about your communication style.
lines.cn: 如你所知，过去几个月里，有人对你的沟通方式提出了一些意见。

lines.t: Of course, we already had like three meetings about this.
lines.cn: 当然，我们为此已经开过三次会了。

lines.t: Look, all I’m going to say is that it was never my intention to offend anyone.
lines.cn: 听着，我要说的只是：我从来无意冒犯任何人。

lines.t: Simply put, I don’t like to write long emails because, frankly, I think they’re a waste of time.
lines.cn: 简单说，我不喜欢写长邮件，因为坦白讲，我觉得那是浪费时间。

lines.t: Conciseness is efficiency.
lines.cn: 简洁就是效率。

lines.t: I feel that writing long emails hurts that same productivity you praised me for just a minute ago.
lines.cn: 我觉得写长邮件恰恰损害了你一分钟前还称赞过的那种效率。

lines.t: And I already apologized if anyone was offended.
lines.cn: 如果冒犯了谁，我已经道过歉了。

lines.t: But to be perfectly honest, I think anyone who was offended was being a little too sensitive.
lines.cn: 但说实话，我认为被冒犯的人都有点太敏感了。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the woman say she has always wanted to do since childhood?

options.A: Provide medical service to the community.
options.B: Make healthcare in her hometown the best.
options.C: Obtain a doctoral degree in internal medicine.
options.D: Have a profound impact on people around her.

questions.cn: 女士说她从小就一直想做什么？

optionsCn.A: 为社区提供医疗服务。
optionsCn.B: 让家乡的医疗条件变成最好的。
optionsCn.C: 取得内科的博士学位。
optionsCn.D: 对身边的人产生深远影响。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman’s parents from the conversation?

options.A: They have constantly urged her to study hard.
options.B: They have worked hard to finance her education.
options.C: They have tried to create a positive learning environment.
options.D: They have pursued the family’s dreams together with her.

questions.cn: 从对话中我们了解到女士的父母什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们一直督促她努力学习。
optionsCn.B: 他们努力工作为她筹措学费。
optionsCn.C: 他们努力营造积极的学习环境。
optionsCn.D: 他们和她一起追逐家庭的梦想。

questions.stem: Why does the woman say she wants to choose internal medicine as her specialty?

options.A: It is a key medical branch conducive to realizing her dreams.
options.B: It connects many other specialties with its broad coverage.
options.C: It has a long history in the man’s prestigious institution.
options.D: It is a medical branch both of her parents specialize in.

questions.cn: 女士为什么说她想选择内科作为专业？

optionsCn.A: 它是有助于她实现梦想的关键医学分支。
optionsCn.B: 它涵盖面广，把许多其他专科联系起来。
optionsCn.C: 它在男士那所名校里历史悠久。
optionsCn.D: 那是她父母双方都专攻的医学分支。

questions.stem: How does the man describe the woman’s school grades?

options.A: Problematic.
options.B: Competitive.
options.C: Inconsistent.
options.D: Trustworthy.

questions.cn: 男士如何形容女士的在校成绩？

optionsCn.A: 有问题。
optionsCn.B: 有竞争力。
optionsCn.C: 不稳定。
optionsCn.D: 值得信赖。

lines.t: So tell me, why do you wish to study medicine?
lines.cn: 那么告诉我，你为什么想学医？

lines.t: I’ve always wanted to be a doctor.
lines.cn: 我一直想当医生。

lines.t: I come from a small town where health care was never the best, and I think that had a profound effect on me.
lines.cn: 我来自一个小镇，那里的医疗条件从来都不算好，我想这对我影响很深。

lines.t: As a child, I remember thinking how great it would be to serve the community and cure people!
lines.cn: 小时候我记得就想过，能服务社区、治病救人该有多好！

lines.t: What other people or events in your life have shaped your interest in becoming a doctor?
lines.cn: 你生活中还有哪些人或事，塑造了你当医生的兴趣？

lines.t: Well, that’s hard to say.
lines.cn: 嗯，这很难说。

lines.t: I would certainly say my parents have been a key factor.
lines.cn: 我肯定会说父母是关键因素。

lines.t: They always pushed me to study hard.
lines.cn: 他们总是督促我努力学习。

lines.t: And I certainly wouldn’t be here without their support.
lines.cn: 没有他们的支持，我肯定不会坐在这里。

lines.t: I guess I was also immensely fortunate to have good teachers and friends around me.
lines.cn: 我想我也特别幸运，身边有好的老师和朋友。

lines.t: At the end of the day, I’ve always been surrounded by a positive environment conducive to my working hard and pursuing my dreams.
lines.cn: 说到底，我一直身处一个积极的环境，有利于我努力学习、追逐梦想。

lines.t: Is there any medical branch that you would like to specialize in?
lines.cn: 有你想专攻的医学分支吗？

lines.t: I haven’t decided yet.
lines.cn: 我还没决定。

lines.t: It’s still early days.
lines.cn: 现在谈这个还为时过早。

lines.t: However, if I had to say, internal medicine.
lines.cn: 不过，如果非要说，是内科。

lines.t: Why internal medicine?
lines.cn: 为什么是内科？

lines.t: I know it’s no picnic.
lines.cn: 我知道这可不容易。

lines.t: But I find it the most intriguing, because it covers so much and ties together so many other specialties.
lines.cn: 但我觉得它最有意思，因为它涵盖面很广，还把许多其他专科串联在一起。

lines.t: Thank you.
lines.cn: 谢谢。

lines.t: Now I’d like to address your academic history and projected grades.
lines.cn: 现在我想谈谈你的学业经历和预期成绩。

lines.t: We like to think of ourselves as a prestigious institution with a highly competitive and promising student body.
lines.cn: 我们希望自己被看作一所名校，学生群体极具竞争力且前途无量。

lines.t: As you know, to get into our programmes, you need at least an 85% score in the entrance exam.
lines.cn: 如你所知，要进入我们的项目，入学考试至少要考到 85%。

lines.t: Do you think you can attain this?
lines.cn: 你觉得你能达到吗？

lines.t: I think so.
lines.cn: 我想可以。

lines.t: Yes.
lines.cn: 是的。

lines.t: I’m looking at your school grades now and I’ll be honest.
lines.cn: 我正在看你的在校成绩，我实话实说。

lines.t: It’s a bit of a mixed bag.
lines.cn: 有点参差不齐。

lines.t: You do get top grades here and there, but you are not very... shall we say, “consistent”?
lines.cn: 你确实这里那里都拿过高分，但你不太……怎么说呢，“稳定”？

lines.t: I see no problem in making you a conditional offer, but consider yourself warned.
lines.cn: 我不介意给你发有条件录取，但你要知道这是有言在先。

lines.t: Our entrance exam is, to use your own words, no picnic.
lines.cn: 我们的入学考试，借用你的话，可不容易。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why do we often have to choose photos that include a street sign to log into our email accounts?

options.A: To prevent hackers from cracking our secret codes.
options.B: To show that all the guidelines are being followed.
options.C: To provide evidence that passwords are forgotten.
options.D: To convince our computer that we are human.

questions.cn: 为什么我们登录邮箱常要挑选带路牌的照片？

optionsCn.A: 防止黑客破解我们的密码。
optionsCn.B: 表明所有指引都得到了遵守。
optionsCn.C: 提供密码被遗忘的证据。
optionsCn.D: 让电脑相信我们是人类。

questions.stem: What do researchers at a university in Finland aim to do in their new study?

options.A: Put an end to the hacking phenomenon.
options.B: Help people remember their passwords.
options.C: Reduce the intricacy of the password itself.
options.D: Explain the need for different email accounts.

questions.cn: 芬兰一所大学的研究者在他们的新研究中想做什么？

optionsCn.A: 终结黑客入侵现象。
optionsCn.B: 帮助人们记住密码。
optionsCn.C: 降低密码本身的复杂度。
optionsCn.D: 解释需要不同邮箱账号的原因。

questions.stem: What do the researchers advise websites to do at the end of the passage?

options.A: Innovate technologies to ensure the safety of users’ accounts.
options.B: Provide incentives for the application of creative passwords.
options.C: Explore the possibility of using simpler secret codes.
options.D: Take steps to encourage users to log in more often.

questions.cn: 研究者在文章最后建议网站怎么做？

optionsCn.A: 创新技术以确保用户账号安全。
optionsCn.B: 为使用有创意的密码提供激励。
optionsCn.C: 探索使用更简单密码的可能性。
optionsCn.D: 采取措施鼓励用户更频繁登录。

lines.t: Logging into your email account can sometimes feel like trying to hack into the Pentagon.
lines.cn: 登录自己的邮箱账号，有时感觉像在试图黑进五角大楼。

lines.t: If you follow all of the guidelines, you need to use a different password for every one of your accounts;
lines.cn: 如果照着所有指引做，你得为每一个账号使用不同的密码；

lines.t: use an incomprehensible variety of letters, numbers, and symbols;
lines.cn: 要用上各种让人看不懂的字母、数字和符号组合；

lines.t: sign up for two-step verification;
lines.cn: 要开通两步验证；

lines.t: and change every password every time one of them is compromised.
lines.cn: 而且只要其中一个密码泄露，就得把所有密码都换一遍。

lines.t: More often than not, you then have to choose photos that include a street sign,
lines.cn: 而且你往往还得从照片里挑出带路牌的，

lines.t: as this apparently provides solid evidence to your computer that you are, in fact, a human being.
lines.cn: 因为据说这能给电脑提供确凿证据，证明你确实是个人类。

lines.t: It’s no small wonder most of us forget our passwords more often than our keys.
lines.cn: 难怪我们大多数人忘掉密码的次数比忘钥匙还多。

lines.t: Now, a new peer-reviewed study by researchers at Aalto University in Finland is attempting to figure out why we forget our passwords in order to help put an end to this frustrating phenomenon.
lines.cn: 如今，芬兰阿尔托大学研究者的一项新同行评审研究试图弄清我们为什么会忘记密码，以帮助终结这一令人抓狂的现象。

lines.t: Their findings suggest that how likely you are to remember your password has less to do with the intricacy of the password itself and more to do with how often you anticipate using it.
lines.cn: 他们的发现表明：你记住密码的可能性，与密码本身的复杂程度关系不大，更多取决于你预计要用它多少次。

lines.t: Which is to say: you are far more likely to remember a complicated password if you know you’ll frequently be using it to log into an account than you are to remember a simple password for an account that you don’t expect to log into very often.
lines.cn: 也就是说：如果你知道自己会经常用某个复杂密码登录某个账号，那你记住它的可能性，要远高于记住一个不常登录账号的简单密码。

lines.t: The researchers advise websites to include more of an incentive for users to log in more often in order to help them remember their secret codes.
lines.cn: 研究者建议网站为用户更频繁登录提供更多激励，以帮助他们记住自己的密码。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What was the problem Jenny Weiner encountered four years ago?

options.A: Her work no longer interested her.
options.B: Her training app did not fit her.
options.C: Her fitness fell into a slump.
options.D: Her business deteriorated.

questions.cn: 四年前珍妮·韦纳遇到的问题是什么？

optionsCn.A: 她的工作不再让她感兴趣。
optionsCn.B: 她的训练应用不适合她。
optionsCn.C: 她的健身陷入了低谷。
optionsCn.D: 她的生意恶化了。

questions.stem: What can the fitness phone app Slimeretics do according to the passage?

options.A: Help users keep track of their fitness levels.
options.B: Design personalized training programmes.
options.C: Strengthen ties among users worldwide.
options.D: Select well-qualified human coaches.

questions.cn: 根据文章，健身手机应用 Slimeretics 能做什么？

optionsCn.A: 帮助用户跟踪自己的健身水平。
optionsCn.B: 设计个性化训练方案。
optionsCn.C: 加强全球用户之间的联系。
optionsCn.D: 挑选合格的真人教练。

questions.stem: Why does the passage say Jenny Weiner now finds the workouts exciting?

options.A: They are never repeated.
options.B: They help enrich her life.
options.C: They are of no extreme intensity.
options.D: They keep her focused on her goal.

questions.cn: 文章为什么说珍妮·韦纳现在觉得训练很带劲？

optionsCn.A: 它们从不重复。
optionsCn.B: 它们帮助丰富她的生活。
optionsCn.C: 它们强度都不算极端。
optionsCn.D: 它们让她专注于目标。

questions.stem: What do some experts think of fitness apps like Slimeretics?

options.A: They will not be able to take the place of human personal trainers.
options.B: They will not be able to comprehend some of the profiles users put in.
options.C: They cannot lead to optimal results with their mathematical approach.
options.D: They cannot match humans in arranging meticulous workout schedules.

questions.cn: 一些专家如何看待 Slimeretics 这类健身应用？

optionsCn.A: 它们无法取代真人私教。
optionsCn.B: 它们无法理解用户输入的部分资料。
optionsCn.C: 它们的数学方法无法带来最佳效果。
optionsCn.D: 它们在安排精细训练计划上比不上人类。

lines.t: Four years ago, Jenny Weiner was in a fitness slump.
lines.cn: 四年前，珍妮·韦纳的健身陷入了低谷。

lines.t: She wanted to improve her physical and mental health.
lines.cn: 她想改善自己的身体和心理健康。

lines.t: However, her workouts lacked intensity without a proper training program to follow.
lines.cn: 然而，没有合适的训练计划可循，她的锻炼缺乏强度。

lines.t: When she went to the gym, her daily ritual predominantly involved easy exercise options like jogging.
lines.cn: 她去健身房时，日常活动主要是一些轻松的锻炼，比如慢跑。

lines.t: She avoided more formidable exercises like lifting weights.
lines.cn: 她回避举重之类更难的项目。

lines.t: A personal trainer who might push her was out of the question.
lines.cn: 能督促她的私人教练想都不用想。

lines.t: The extravagant cost was just unaffordable.
lines.cn: 那高昂的费用她根本负担不起。

lines.t: She then discovered the fitness phone app Slimeretics.
lines.cn: 后来她发现了健身手机应用 Slimeretics。

lines.t: To use the app, you first input your profile about your previous training experiences and preferences, as well as your desired goals.
lines.cn: 使用这个应用，你要先输入自己的资料：过往训练经历、偏好，以及期望达成的目标。

lines.t: A virtual coach then uses that information to suggest a personalised training regime.
lines.cn: 随后一位虚拟教练会利用这些信息推荐个性化的训练方案。

lines.t: After the workout, the app’s artificial intelligence software system uses feedback from Ms. Weiner and its other 53 million users around the world to adjust future training sessions.
lines.cn: 训练结束后，该应用的人工智能软件系统会结合韦纳女士及全球其他 5300 万用户的反馈，调整未来的训练安排。

lines.t: Now Ms. Weiner finds the workouts exciting.
lines.cn: 如今韦纳女士觉得训练很带劲。

lines.t: This is because no two are ever the same.
lines.cn: 因为每次训练都不一样。

lines.t: As a result, the app has helped her to lose more than 25 kilograms.
lines.cn: 结果，这个应用帮她减掉了 25 公斤以上。

lines.t: The app’s mathematical approach can arrange a more meticulous workout schedule.
lines.cn: 该应用的数学方法能安排更精细的训练计划。

lines.t: This has led to optimal results.
lines.cn: 这带来了最佳效果。

lines.t: However, some experts think that apps cannot replace human personal trainers.
lines.cn: 然而，一些专家认为应用无法取代真人私教。

lines.t: An app cannot understand human behavior.
lines.cn: 应用无法理解人的行为。

lines.t: It will not comprehend that there are competing interests outside of health and fitness.
lines.cn: 它不会明白，健康与健身之外还有相互竞争的各种利益。

lines.t: Additionally, a human trainer can add compassion to the workout.
lines.cn: 此外，真人教练能为训练注入关怀。

lines.t: He can also make exercise fun and sustainable.
lines.cn: 他还能让锻炼变得有趣且可持续。

lines.t: Trainers can monitor whether a person is doing exercises correctly.
lines.cn: 教练可以监督一个人动作是否做得正确。

lines.t: This can safeguard against injuries.
lines.cn: 这能防止受伤。

lines.t: An app cannot perceive such subtleties.
lines.cn: 应用无法察觉这类细微之处。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn from the conclusion of the Oxford University researchers?

options.A: All societies are built upon the cornerstones of basic values.
options.B: Everyone everywhere demonstrates seven character traits.
options.C: All societies are kept together by seven basic moral rules.
options.D: Everyone everywhere shares a universal moral standard.

questions.cn: 从牛津大学研究者的结论中我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 所有社会都建立在基本价值观的基石之上。
optionsCn.B: 各地每个人都展现出七种品格特质。
optionsCn.C: 所有社会都由七条基本道德准则维系在一起。
optionsCn.D: 各地每个人都共享一套普世道德标准。

questions.stem: What did the new study by Oxford researchers aim to do?

options.A: Ascertain whether deferring to authority was confined to right-wing people.
options.B: Find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.
options.C: Make clear whether all societies faced the same moral issues.
options.D: Find out whether left-wing people still had a group loyalty.

questions.cn: 牛津研究者的新研究旨在做什么？

optionsCn.A: 查明敬重权威是否只限于右翼人士。
optionsCn.B: 弄清不同社会是否有不同版本的道德。
optionsCn.C: 弄清楚是否所有社会都面对相同的道德问题。
optionsCn.D: 查明左翼人士是否仍有群体忠诚。

questions.stem: What does Harvey Whitehouse think social scientists should do to test theories of morality?

options.A: Make independent descriptions of cultures around the world.
options.B: Strive to understand the basic differences between peoples.
options.C: Appreciate the foundational value of the existing data.
options.D: Carry out systematic field studies to gather new data.

questions.cn: 哈维·怀特豪斯认为社会科学家应该怎么做来检验道德理论？

optionsCn.A: 对世界各地文化做出独立的描述。
optionsCn.B: 努力理解各民族之间的根本差异。
optionsCn.C: 珍视既有数据的基础价值。
optionsCn.D: 开展系统的实地研究以收集新数据。

lines.t: All societies are held together by seven universal moral rules, which include deferring to superiors and respecting the property of others, Oxford University has concluded.
lines.cn: 牛津大学的研究得出结论：所有社会都由七条普世道德准则维系在一起，其中包括敬重上级和尊重他人财产。

lines.t: Although many cultures are moving towards more liberal, less hierarchical organizations, the new research suggests that traditional power structures and basic values of charity and brotherhood are the cornerstones of successful societies.
lines.cn: 尽管许多文化正走向更自由、等级更淡化的组织形式，这项新研究仍表明，传统的权力结构以及慈善与手足情谊的基本价值观，是成功社会的基石。

lines.t: The huge study of 60 different cultures around the world found that all communities operate under seven basic moral codes.
lines.cn: 这项对全球 60 种不同文化的大型研究发现，所有社群都在七条基本道德准则下运作。

lines.t: Those universal rules are: help your family, help your group, return favours, be brave, defer to superiors, divide resources fairly and respect the property of others.
lines.cn: 这些普世准则包括：帮助家人、帮助本群体、回报恩惠、勇敢、敬重上级、公平分配资源、尊重他人财产。

lines.t: The character traits held for every kind of community, be they traditional hunter-gatherers or advanced civilizations, helping to uphold civilised society and foster social cooperation, researchers found.
lines.cn: 研究者发现，无论是传统的狩猎采集者还是发达文明，这些品格特质都为各类社群所持有，有助于维系文明社会、促进社会合作。

lines.t: “Everyone everywhere shares a common moral code,” said Dr. Oliver Scott Curry, lead author and senior researcher at Oxford.
lines.cn: 论文第一作者、牛津大学高级研究员奥利弗·斯科特·柯里博士说：“各地所有人都共享着一套共同的道德准则。”

lines.t: “These seven moral rules appear to be universal across cultures because people face the same social problems.
lines.cn: “这七条道德准则在不同文化中似乎是普世的，因为人们面对的是相同的社会问题。

lines.t: Even if some of these traits look right-wing or conservative, for example, deferring to authority, left-wing people will still have a group loyalty and deference to someone or something.
lines.cn: 即便其中某些特质看起来偏右派或保守，比如敬重权威，左翼人士同样会有群体忠诚，也会对某人或某事保持敬重。

lines.t: This shows there really is more that unites us than divides us.”
lines.cn: 这说明，把我们联结起来的共性，确实多于把我们分开的分歧。”

lines.t: The study, published in Current Anthropology, is the largest and most comprehensive and widespread survey of morals ever conducted and aimed to find out whether different societies had different versions of morality.
lines.cn: 这项发表在《当代人类学》上的研究，是迄今规模最大、最全面、覆盖最广的道德调查，旨在弄清不同社会是否有不同版本的道德。

lines.t: The team accessed the world’s best archives to analyze accounts from more than 600 sources of 60 societies around the world.
lines.cn: 研究团队查阅了世界一流档案，分析了全球 60 个社会、600 多个来源的记述。

lines.t: They found that the seven rules were considered morally good in all societies and were observed across all continents, religions, and politics.
lines.cn: 他们发现，这七条准则在所有社会都被视为道德上的善，并在所有大洲、宗教和政治制度中都能观察到。

lines.t: However, some communities valued certain rules more highly than others.
lines.cn: 不过，有些社群对某些准则的重视程度高于其他准则。

lines.t: Dr. Curry hopes that this research helps to promote mutual understanding between people of different cultures and appreciation of what we have in common and how and why we differ.
lines.cn: 柯里博士希望这项研究有助于促进不同文化背景的人相互理解，认识我们的共同之处，以及我们为何、如何存在差异。

lines.t: Co-author Professor Harvey Whitehouse, said social scientists should now set about testing the theory in the field, rather than relying on old data.
lines.cn: 合著者哈维·怀特豪斯教授说，社会科学家现在应当着手在实地检验这一理论，而不是依赖旧数据。

lines.t: “This study was based on historical descriptions of cultures around the world,” he said.
lines.cn: 他说：“这项研究基于对世界各地文化的历史描述。”

lines.t: “these descriptions were made independent of and prior to the theory we’re testing.”
lines.cn: “这些描述是独立于、并先于我们要检验的理论而产生的。”

lines.t: In future, if social scientists are serious about testing theories of morality, they will need to gather new data, more systematically, out in the field.
lines.cn: 今后，如果社会科学家要严肃检验道德理论，就需要在实地上更系统地收集新数据。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about our eyes?

options.A: They might be the most important part of our eating experience.
options.B: They can activate our brain functions in a most direct fashion.
options.C: They can be viewed as the windows to our soul.
options.D: They could mislead us in more ways than one.

questions.cn: 关于我们的眼睛，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们可能是我们进食体验中最重要的部分。
optionsCn.B: 它们能以最直接的方式激活我们的大脑功能。
optionsCn.C: 它们可以被看作我们灵魂的窗户。
optionsCn.D: 它们可能在不止一个方面误导我们。

questions.stem: What does color actually do according to this lecture?

options.A: It attracts food companies’ growing attention.
options.B: It adversely impacts one’s eating experience.
options.C: It invariably determines how food sells.
options.D: It changes the way people taste food.

questions.cn: 根据这堂课，颜色实际上起什么作用？

optionsCn.A: 它吸引食品公司越来越多的关注。
optionsCn.B: 它对一个人的进食体验产生不利影响。
optionsCn.C: 它总是决定食物的销售情况。
optionsCn.D: 它改变人们品尝食物的方式。

questions.stem: What does the brain use color to do?

options.A: Enhance the taste.
options.B: Make predictions.
options.C: Identify distinct flavors.
options.D: Enrich the eating experience.

questions.cn: 大脑利用颜色来做什么？

optionsCn.A: 增强味道。
optionsCn.B: 做出预测。
optionsCn.C: 识别不同的风味。
optionsCn.D: 丰富进食体验。

lines.t: When it comes to food, color is money.
lines.cn: 在食品上，颜色就是钱。

lines.t: Food companies know that better color gives better prices.
lines.cn: 食品公司知道，颜色更好就能卖更好的价钱。

lines.t: So they ensure that their products are attractive in color to bolster earnings.
lines.cn: 因此他们确保自家产品在颜色上吸引人，以提升收益。

lines.t: Oranges, for example, have to meet specific color standards.
lines.cn: 比如橙子，就必须符合特定的颜色标准。

lines.t: And oranges are just the beginning.
lines.cn: 而这只是开始。

lines.t: There are color standards for foods, including French fries, tomatoes, pumpkins, olives, honey, and cherries.
lines.cn: 包括炸薯条、西红柿、南瓜、橄榄、蜂蜜和樱桃在内的许多食品都有颜色标准。

lines.t: The attention to color is for good reason.
lines.cn: 对颜色的重视是有充分理由的。

lines.t: For all the talk of the tongue, our eyes really might be the most important part of the eating experience.
lines.cn: 尽管人们总在谈论舌头，我们的眼睛或许才是进食体验中最重要的部分。

lines.t: A great number of our brain functions are dedicated to processing vision, while only a percent or two is given over to taste faculties.
lines.cn: 我们大脑的大量功能都用于处理视觉，而用于味觉的只有百分之一二。

lines.t: And the result is that color actually changes how we taste food.
lines.cn: 结果就是，颜色实际上会改变我们品尝食物的方式。

lines.t: Scientists have demonstrated many times the importance of color to taste.
lines.cn: 科学家已多次证明颜色对味觉的重要性。

lines.t: In a 1980 study, for example, test participants were asked to name the flavor of the beverage they were drinking without being able to see that beverage.
lines.cn: 例如 1980 年的一项研究中，受试者被要求在看不清饮料的情况下说出所喝饮料的味道。

lines.t: Only one in five was able to identify it as orange.
lines.cn: 只有五分之一的人辨认出是橙子味。

lines.t: But when they were allowed to see what they were drinking, which was orange in color, each of them identified the orange flavor.
lines.cn: 但当允许他们看到所喝的东西——颜色是橙色的——每个人都认出了橙子味。

lines.t: And when a drink that was lime flavor was colored orange, nearly half of respondents identified the flavor of the beverage as orange.
lines.cn: 而当一杯青柠味饮料被调成橙色时，近一半受访者把它的味道说成橙子味。

lines.t: None made that mistake when the beverage was green in color.
lines.cn: 当饮料呈绿色时，没有人犯这个错误。

lines.t: What’s happening when someone fails to identify the flavor of a beverage they can’t see or that has an abnormal color?
lines.cn: 当一个人无法辨认看不见或颜色异常的饮料的味道时，究竟发生了什么？

lines.t: Is it that participants can’t discern what the flavor is, and so rely on visual cues?
lines.cn: 是受试者分辨不出味道，于是依赖视觉线索？

lines.t: Or does color actually change the experience of taste?
lines.cn: 还是颜色真的改变了味觉体验？

lines.t: The key to these questions is the effect of color on expectation.
lines.cn: 这些问题的关键在于颜色对预期的影响。

lines.t: The brain makes predictions using color.
lines.cn: 大脑会利用颜色做出预测。

lines.t: These predictions rely on expectations that come from experience.
lines.cn: 这些预测依赖来自经验的预期。

lines.t: Research shows that we’re all born liking sweet things and desire to eat them, but we aren’t born knowing what the sweet things we crave look like.
lines.cn: 研究显示，我们天生就喜欢甜食、想吃甜食，但我们并非生来就知道自己渴望的甜食长什么样。

lines.t: So we need to learn this over time.
lines.cn: 所以我们得随着时间慢慢学会。

lines.t: The brain gets information from the environment, and we learn, for example, that fruits go from green and sour to red and ripe and sweet.
lines.cn: 大脑从环境中获取信息，比如我们学会水果从青涩酸口变成红艳成熟而甘甜。

lines.t: Thus, if we see a green berry, we equate its color with a sour taste, and just looking at a red fruit will activate our expectations that it will taste sweet and delicious.
lines.cn: 因此，看到一颗绿色的浆果，我们就把它的颜色等同于酸味；而只要看到红色水果，就会激活它尝起来香甜可口的预期。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say many of us search for throughout our lives?

options.A: Social status.
options.B: Financial resources.
options.C: Meaning.
options.D: Happiness.

questions.cn: 讲话者说我们许多人在一生中寻找什么？

optionsCn.A: 社会地位。
optionsCn.B: 财务资源。
optionsCn.C: 意义。
optionsCn.D: 幸福。

questions.stem: What do Rhia Catapano and colleagues find about economic resources?

options.A: Their effect on people’s happiness has long been overstated.
options.B: Their influence on people’s life varies with social contexts.
options.C: They can affect people’s experience of meaning.
options.D: They can ensure people’s overall wellbeing.

questions.cn: 关于经济资源，里娅·卡塔帕诺及其同事发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们对人们幸福的影响长期被夸大。
optionsCn.B: 它们对人们生活的影响随社会情境而异。
optionsCn.C: 它们会影响人们对意义的体验。
optionsCn.D: 它们能保障人们的整体福祉。

questions.stem: What do we learn about Rhia Catapano and colleagues’ second study?

options.A: It used questions totally different from those in their first study.
options.B: It focused on the sense of meaning of French participants.
options.C: It analysed cases from a daily poll of US residents.
options.D: It examined data collected from multiple countries.

questions.cn: 关于里娅·卡塔帕诺及其同事的第二项研究，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它使用的问题与第一项研究完全不同。
optionsCn.B: 它关注法国受访者的意义感。
optionsCn.C: 它分析了美国居民每日调查的案例。
optionsCn.D: 它考察了从多个国家收集的数据。

questions.stem: Why do meaning and happiness have a weaker relationship in those with more resources?

options.A: They might have more access to external sources of happiness.
options.B: They might focus on an individual sense of satisfaction or meaning.
options.C: They might be less easily affected by a community’s overall feeling.
options.D: They might be less adversely impacted by failure to achieve a purpose.

questions.cn: 为什么在资源较多的人身上，意义与幸福的关系较弱？

optionsCn.A: 他们可能有更多外部的幸福来源。
optionsCn.B: 他们可能专注于个人的满足感或意义感。
optionsCn.C: 他们可能更不容易受社群整体情绪影响。
optionsCn.D: 他们可能更不容易因未达成目标而受不良影响。

lines.t: Searching for meaning is something many of us experience throughout our lives.
lines.cn: 寻找意义，是我们许多人一生中都会经历的事。

lines.t: For some, this meaning is religious; some political; and some interpersonal.
lines.cn: 对一些人来说，这意义是宗教性的；一些人是政治性的；还有一些是人际层面的。

lines.t: And having a sense of meaning can bring us happiness.
lines.cn: 而拥有意义感能带给我们幸福。

lines.t: A new study looks at the relationship between meaning and happiness in the context of financial resources.
lines.cn: 一项新研究在财务资源的背景下考察了意义与幸福之间的关系。

lines.t: Rhia Catapano from the University of Toronto and colleagues find meaning is a far weaker predictor of happiness for rich people than poorer people—suggesting economic resources can impact how we experience meaning.
lines.cn: 多伦多大学的里娅·卡塔帕诺及其同事发现，对富有人群来说，意义对幸福的预测力远弱于较贫穷的人——这表明经济资源会影响我们体验意义的方式。

lines.t: The team analysed data from over 500,000 people across 123 countries.
lines.cn: 研究团队分析了 123 个国家、50 多万人的数据。

lines.t: The first study used data from a daily poll of US residents collected between 2013 and 2015.
lines.cn: 第一项研究使用 2013 至 2015 年间一项针对美国居民的每日调查数据。

lines.t: Well-being was tracked using measures of positive affect—whether, during the day before they were surveyed, participants had smiled or laughed a lot, or experienced a lot of happiness.
lines.cn: 幸福感用积极情绪指标衡量——即受访者在被调查的前一天是否经常微笑或大笑，或体验到大量快乐。

lines.t: Meaning was measured through a daily “purpose index”, which explored the extent to which participants felt that they like what they do every day and are motivated to achieve their goals.
lines.cn: 意义感则通过每日“目标指数”衡量，考察受访者在多大程度上觉得自己喜欢每天所做的事，并有动力去实现目标。

lines.t: Finally, income levels were assessed.
lines.cn: 最后，评估了收入水平。

lines.t: The results showed that the correlation between meaning and happiness was strongest among those in lower income brackets.
lines.cn: 结果显示，意义与幸福之间的相关性在低收入群体中最强。

lines.t: But as income levels increased, the correlation became weaker.
lines.cn: 但随着收入水平升高，这种相关性变弱。

lines.t: The second study looked at worldwide data.
lines.cn: 第二项研究考察了全球数据。

lines.t: Happiness was measured using the same questions as in the first study, while meaning was measured using the single question: “Do you feel your life has an important purpose or meaning?”
lines.cn: 幸福感用与第一项研究相同的问题衡量，意义感则用一个问题衡量：“你觉得自己的生活有重要的目的或意义吗？”

lines.t: Again, the strength of the relationship between meaning and happiness depended on participants’ income: meaning had a greater influence on happiness for those on lower incomes compared to those in higher brackets.
lines.cn: 同样，意义与幸福之间关系的强度取决于受访者的收入：与高收入群体相比，意义对低收入者的幸福影响更大。

lines.t: In the final study, French participants indicated the extent to which they felt they led a purposeful and meaningful life and how much they considered themselves a happy person.
lines.cn: 在最后一项研究中，法国受访者指出自己在多大程度上觉得自己过着有目标、有意义的生活，以及自己在多大程度上认为自己是个幸福的人。

lines.t: Finally, rather than using specific income brackets, they placed themselves on a “social ladder”, representing where they stand in society with regard to wealth, education, and career.
lines.cn: 最后，他们没有使用具体收入区间，而是在一条“社会阶梯”上标明自己的位置，代表自己在财富、教育和职业方面所处的社会地位。

lines.t: The results from this study duplicated those of the first two.
lines.cn: 这项研究的结果与前两项一致。

lines.t: So, overall, meaning and happiness had a stronger relationship in those with fewer resources than those with more.
lines.cn: 所以总体而言，意义与幸福的关系在资源较少的人身上比资源较多的人更强。

lines.t: This might be the case because richer individuals have more access to other sources of happiness—many of which will be external, like lack of stress or community.
lines.cn: 这可能是因为更富有的人有更多其他幸福来源——其中许多是外部的，比如没有压力或社区支持。

lines.t: Thus, a focus on an internal sense of satisfaction, purpose, or meaning is less important.
lines.cn: 因此，对内在的满足感、目标感或意义感的关注就没那么重要。
